cohort: The study included 203 patients who underwent robotic sacrocolpopexy and 291 patients who underwent abdominal sacrocolpopexy at the study hospital between July 1, 2018 and May 31, 2022.
finding: Abdominal sacrocolpopexy was associated with lower costs and higher reimbursement rates than robotic sacrocolpopexy, leading to a higher profit margin for the hospital, despite longer hospital stays and slightly higher estimated blood loss.
